title: C482/2349/2023 of GULAM GAUS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
UKHC010194632023
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No. 2349 of 2023
1. Gulam Gaus
2: Tariqhulla Khan
3: Mohd. Yunus Salmani alias Yunus Usmani
--Applicants
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and Another
--Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. M.K. Ray, learned counsel with Mr. Harsh Taneja, learned
counsel for the applicants.
Mr. Chitrarth Kandpal, learned Brief Holder for the State/
respondent no.1.
Ms. Farheen Bano, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. Tijil
Gangwar, learned counsel for the respondent no.2.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. M. K. Ray, learned counsel for the
applicants.
Mr. Chitrarth Kandpal, learned Brief Holder for
the State/respondent no.1.
Ms. Farheen Bano, learned counsel holding
brief of Mr. Tijil Gangwar, learned counsel for the
respondent no.2.
2. By means of the present Criminal Misc.
Application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., the applicants
have sought quashing of the impugned charge sheet
dated 29.09.2023 and cognizance/summoning order
dated 03.11.2023 as well as the entire proceedings of
Special Sessions Trial No.963 of 2023, 'State vs. Gulam
Gaus and Others", under Sections 504, 506 of IPC and
1

UKHC010194632023
Section 3(1)(r) of the Scheduled Castes and the
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989,
Police Station Gadarpur, District Udham Singh Nagar,
pending before the court of learned Special Sessions
Judge, Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar.
3. During the pendency of the instant Criminal Misc.
application before this Court, the applicants and the
respondent no.2 have jointly filed a Compounding
Application (No.03 of 2026) with the prayer that this
instant application may be allowed and impugned charge
sheet dated 29.09.2023 and cognizance/summoning
order dated 03.11.2023 as well as the entire proceedings
of Special Sessions Trial No.963 of 2023, 'State vs.
Gulam Gaus and Others", under Sections 504, 506 of
IPC and Section 3(1)(r) of the Scheduled Castes and the
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, at
police station Gadarpur, District Udham Singh Nagar
pending before the court of learned Special Sessions
Judge, Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar may be
quashed.
4. Applicant no.1-Gulam Gaus, applicant no.2-
Tariqhulla Khan and applicant no.3-Mohd. Yunus are
present. They are duly identified by Mr. M.K. Ray,
Advocate.
5. The respondent no.2 - Rajat alias Ashwini
2

UKHC010194632023
Kumar is also present in-person. He is duly identified by
Ms. Farheen Bano, Advocate.
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties on
Compounding Application (IA No.03 of 2026).
7. The said application is duly supported by the
affidavits of the applicant no.1, applicant no.2, applicant
no.3 on the one side and the respondent no.2-
victim/complainant on the other side.
8. On an interaction with the complainant/
respondent no.2 Mr. Rajat alias Ashwani Kumar, he has
stated before the Court that the parties have entered into
a compromise on their own free will and without any
pressure, and the parties belong to the same city and
they want to reside peacefully, and does not want to
prosecute the applicants arising out of the said criminal
case. They want to maintain peace and harmony between
them and thus submit that the matter may be closed and
the compounding application may be allowed.
9. The Court also interacted with the applicants:
Applicants Gulam Gaus, Tariqhullah Khan, Mohammad
Yunus Salmani alias Yunus Salmani. The applicants also
state that the parties have entered into a compromise,
and the opposite party does not want to prosecute the
applicants any longer and they submit that the
compounding application may be allowed.
3

UKHC010194632023
10. Learned counsel for the applicants and the
respondent no.2 thus urge that the compounding
application be allowed and the impugned charge sheet,
cognizance/summoning order and entire proceedings of
the said Special Sessions Trial may be quashed.
11. However, on the other side, learned Brief
Holder for the State would submit that the offenses
punishable under Section 3(1)(r) the SC & ST Act, which
is non-compoundable, and thus would submit that
respondent no.2 may not be permitted to compound the
offences, and the compounding application may be
rejected.
12. On this, learned counsel for the applicant
would submit that this Court has consistently permitted
compounding in SC/ST matters. He has relied upon
judgments of this Court in the case of Pappu Negi alias
Girish Negi & Another vs. State of Uttarakhand &
Another, reported in 2017 SCC OnLine Utt 700; Rajesh
Kumar & Four Others vs. State of Uttarakhand &
Another, reported in 2017 SCC OnLine Utt 1083; and
Manish Chauhan & Others vs. State of Uttarakhand &
Another, reported in 2017 SCC OnLine Utt 237 and he
would submit that in all these aforesaid matters, this
Court has consistently allowed compounding applications
and have quashed proceedings under the SC/ST Act.
4

UKHC010194632023
13. In this regard, reference is made to the
judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Gian
Singh vs. State of Punjab, 2012 (10) SCC 303, Dimpey
Gujral vs. Union Territory, Chandigarh, (2013) 11 SCC
497, B.S. Joshi vs. State of Haryana, (2003) 4 SCC 675
and Nikhil Merchant vs. CBI, (2008) 9 SCC 677, wherein
the Hon'ble Supreme Court has permitted the
compounding of non-compoundable offences.
14. In such view of the matter, the objection as
raised by the learned Brief Holder for the State is
unsustainable. Therefore, since the parties have entered
into a compromise and they want to reside peacefully,
and particularly the respondent no.2 does not want to
pursue the matter any longer, it would be a futile
exercise to let the matter go into trial. Therefore,
compounding application is allowed, and the offences are
permitted to be compounded.
15. As a consequence thereof, the impugned
charge sheet dated 29.09.2023 and cognizance/
summoning order dated 03.11.2023 as well as the entire
proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No.963 of 2023,
'State vs. Gulam Gaus and Others", under Sections 504,
506 of IPC and Section 3(1)(r) of the Scheduled Castes
and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
1989, Police Station Gadarpur, District Udham Singh
5

UKHC010194632023
Nagar pending before the court of learned Special
Sessions Judge, Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar
are hereby quashed.
16. The Criminal Misc. Application No.2349 of
2023 is, accordingly, disposed of.
17. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of
accordingly.
 (Siddhartha Sah, J.)
